data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the decentralized network 'naturally introduces heterogeneity' but this is empirically unsubstantiated and contradicted by its own countercondition acknowledging convergence on an industry-standard stack. The covering principle it relies on — that independence of operators yields architectural distance — does not hold under economic pressures toward standardization. By baking 'provided the network maintains high Architectural Distance' into the claim, it effectively assumes the conclusion: resilience holds if the very property that creates resilience is present, leaving the original claim (decentralized is more resilient) without an unconditional argument.
